title: Iterating a custom collection
hints: All returns an iter.Seq2[int, T]: its yield takes two values, the index and the element, which a range loop receives as `for i, v := range list.All()`.

Walk the linked list from head, following next pointers, and keep a counter for the index. Backward is easier from a slice: collect the values first, then yield them in reverse. Stop whenever yield returns false.
All: i := 0; for n := l.head; n != nil; n = n.next { if !yield(i, n.val) { return }; i++ }. Backward: vals := slices.Collect(l.Values()), then loop from the end.
